title: DHCP Systems: Enterprise Connectivity
description: Welcome to the DHCP Core Lab. As a Systems Administrator, your goal is to maintain the 'Invisible Infrastructure.' When DHCP works, no one notices; when it fails, the entire network grinds to a halt.
reportOverview: This report documents your ability to identify common DHCP failure points including scope exhaustion, unauthorized servers, and incorrect option delivery.

intro.objective: To master the DORA process (Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge) and manage the specialized configuration options that modern enterprise devices require to function.
intro.scenario: You are managing the network for 'Global-Tech Inc.' The environment consists of several VLANs, a mix of Windows and Linux clients, and an aging VOIP phone system. Your task is to resolve the daily influx of connectivity tickets using an evidence-first approach.
workflow_tips: Check the 'Artifacts' first—look for APIPA addresses (169.254.x.x) which indicate a total failure to reach a server.
Pay attention to Subnet Masks and Gateways; an IP address alone isn't enough for internet access.
Remember that routers block broadcasts; if a new wing is offline, the 'Helper' might be missing.

tickets.title: Unusual Gateway Assignment
tickets.summary: Multiple users on the Marketing floor are reporting they can't reach internal resources, but they seem to be able to reach personal email sites. Their IPs look 'off'.
artifact: Physical Check: A small white plastic device found plugged into Wall Jack 402.

triage.q: What is the most immediate conclusion based on the client receiving a 192.168.x.x address on a 10.x.x.x network?
options: The main DHCP server has failed and failed over to a backup range
The client has a static IP set by the user
A 'Rogue' DHCP server (likely a home router) is responding on the wire
The network switch has rebooted into safe mode

diagnosis.q: Why did the client machine accept the 192.168.1.1 gateway instead of the corporate one?
options: The rogue server responded to the DHCP Discover broadcast faster than the corporate server
The corporate server is configured to ignore the Marketing floor
Windows always prefers 192.168 addresses over 10.x addresses
The rogue server has a higher priority 'metric' in Active Directory

fix.q: What is the best long-term remediation to prevent this from happening again on this floor?
options: Change the corporate subnet to 192.168.1.0/24
Enable 'DHCP Snooping' on the access layer switches
Disable the DHCP service on the Domain Controller
Tell users not to bring devices from home

debrief.summary: A rogue DHCP server (like a home router) can cause 'split brain' networks where clients get incorrect gateways.
debrief.takeaway: DHCP Snooping is a Layer 2 security feature that only allows DHCP 'Offers' from trusted switch ports.

tickets.title: The 'Lunch Break' Disconnect
tickets.summary: Every day at 1:00 PM, users returning from the guest lobby complain they can no longer connect to the Wi-Fi. It works fine for the first 20 people in the morning.
artifact: Traffic Pattern: High turnover (guests staying 30-60 mins)

triage.q: What do the Scope Statistics (253 In-Use) reveal about the current issue?
options: The server is running too slow to process requests
The IP address pool is exhausted and cannot fulfill new requests
The subnet mask is incorrectly configured
There is a broadcast storm on the wireless network

diagnosis.q: Given the high turnover of guests, why are addresses not being reclaimed when people leave?
options: Guests are not clicking 'Logout' on the portal
The 8-day lease duration is keeping IPs reserved long after guests leave
The server database is corrupted and won't delete old entries
The router is blocking 'Release' packets from smartphones

fix.q: What configuration change will solve this without changing the network size?
options: Shorten the Lease Duration to 2 or 4 hours
Increase the Lease Duration to 30 days to ensure stability
Change the subnet to a /16
Disable the DHCP server during lunch hours

debrief.summary: Lease duration should match user behavior. Transient areas (Lobbies, Cafes) need short leases to recycle IPs quickly.
debrief.takeaway: Avoid the 'default' 8-day lease for high-turnover wireless segments.

tickets.title: Internal App 404s
tickets.summary: Users can reach 'google.com' but cannot reach the internal portal 'kb.corp.local'. They are getting a 404 or 'Server Not Found' error.

triage.q: What is the problem with the DNS servers assigned to the client?
options: The DNS servers are too slow
Public DNS (8.8.8.8) cannot resolve internal (.local) names
The client is using IPv6 instead of IPv4
The DNS server IPs are missing from the gateway

diagnosis.q: Where is the client getting these external DNS addresses from?
options: The web browser's hardcoded settings
DHCP Option 006 (DNS Servers) is configured with public IPs
The computer's BIOS settings
The ISP's modem

fix.q: How do you ensure all clients use the internal DNS server?
options: Update DHCP Option 006 to point to 10.10.10.10
Tell users to manually change their DNS to 10.10.10.10
Add a forwarder on the Google DNS servers
Disable the DHCP service

debrief.summary: DHCP doesn't just give out IPs; it gives out the 'identity' of the network (DNS, WINS, NTP).
debrief.takeaway: Always point internal clients to internal DNS first so they can find Active Directory resources.

tickets.title: The 'Flipping' Printer
tickets.summary: The main reception printer is intermittently going offline. Some days it works, other days it is 'Unreachable'.
artifact: DHCP Audit Log: 'Address 10.0.0.25 issued to workstation-04'

triage.q: What does the Audit Log reveal about the printer's IP address?
options: The printer is turning itself off
The DHCP server is issuing the printer's IP to other devices
The printer has a bad network cable
The DHCP server is offline

diagnosis.q: Why is the DHCP server giving away an address that the printer is already using?
options: The printer didn't 'tell' the server it was using it
The static IP was set within the dynamic range without an exclusion or reservation
The workstation-04 has 'Admin' rights
The subnet mask is too long

fix.q: How do you permanently prevent this conflict?
options: Create a DHCP Reservation for the printer's MAC at 10.0.0.25
Restart the printer every morning
Change the workstation's IP manually
Increase the DHCP lease time

debrief.summary: Static IPs should always be excluded from the pool OR managed via DHCP Reservations.
debrief.takeaway: If a device is 'important' enough for a static IP, the DHCP server needs to know so it doesn't give it to a random laptop.

tickets.title: Phones Stuck on 'Waiting for DHCP'
tickets.summary: The company just deployed 50 new IP phones. They are powered on and plugged in, but they never get past the 'Configuring' screen.

triage.q: What specific piece of information are the phones missing from the DHCP server?
options: A default gateway
The address of the TFTP server (Option 66)
A valid subnet mask
A DNS suffix

diagnosis.q: Most IP phones require 'DHCP Options' to find their configuration files. Which option is standard for Boot Server Host Names?
options: Option 003
Option 006
Option 066
Option 015

fix.q: What change should be made in the DHCP console?
options: Add Option 066 and enter the IP of the Phone Controller/TFTP server
Create a new scope for the phones only
Disable Windows Firewall on the DHCP server
Give the phones static IPs one by one

debrief.summary: Advanced devices (Phones, Thin Clients, PXE boot) use DHCP Options to find their config servers automatically.
debrief.takeaway: Option 66 (TFTP Server) and Option 67 (Bootfile Name) are critical for VOIP and Imaging.

tickets.title: New Wing, No Signal
tickets.summary: A new office wing was added with its own subnet (10.20.1.0/24). Computers there get 169.254.x.x, but if you carry them back to the old wing, they work fine.
artifact: Router: New Wing and Old Wing are separated by a Layer 3 Switch

triage.q: Why are the clients in the new wing getting APIPA (169.254) addresses?
options: The DHCP server is out of IPs
The DHCP Discover broadcasts are not reaching the server across the router
The network cable is too long
The clients are not authorized to use the new wing

diagnosis.q: What feature must be enabled on the Layer 3 switch to 'help' these requests reach the server?
options: A Static Route
A DHCP Relay Agent (IP Helper)
An Access Control List
Port Mirroring

fix.q: What command should be applied to the New Wing's Gateway interface?
options: ip helper-address 10.10.1.5
shutdown / restart
dhcp-enable

debrief.summary: Routers block broadcasts. DHCP is a broadcast protocol.
debrief.takeaway: The IP Helper address 'converts' the broadcast into a unicast packet and sends it directly to the server.

tickets.title: The CEO's New Laptop
tickets.summary: The CEO has a brand new laptop. It works at his house, but in the office, it just says 'Identifying...' and never connects.
artifact: Audit Log: 'Packet dropped - MAC 00-1A-2B... - Denied by filter'

triage.q: What is the DHCP server doing with the CEO's request according to the log?
options: The server is ignoring it because the MAC address is not on the 'Allow' list
The server is trying to send an IP but the laptop is rejecting it
The server is out of memory
The server is not authorized in AD

diagnosis.q: Why are other employees working fine?
options: They have faster computers
Their MAC addresses were already added to the 'Allow' filter list
They are using static IPs
They are on a different VLAN

fix.q: What is the fix to get the CEO online immediately?
options: Add the CEO's MAC address to the 'Allow' filter folder in the DHCP console
Disable the entire DHCP server and restart it
Tell the CEO to use his phone's hotspot
Delete the DHCP database

debrief.summary: DHCP Filters allow you to whitelist or blacklist specific hardware (MAC) addresses.
debrief.takeaway: If 'Allow' filters are on, every new device must be manually registered or it will be ignored.

tickets.title: New Server, No Service
tickets.summary: You've just promoted a new Windows Server and installed the DHCP role. You created a scope, but it's showing a red down arrow and won't start.
artifact: DHCP Console: Red Down Arrow on IPv4 Node
Event Viewer: ID 1046 'The DHCP service is not authorized to start'

triage.q: What is the meaning of a red down arrow even when the Windows service is 'Started'?
options: The database is corrupt
The server lacks authorization in Active Directory
The scope is empty
The network cable is unplugged

diagnosis.q: In an AD Domain, who has the right to authorize a DHCP server?
options: Any Domain User
An Enterprise Administrator
A Help Desk Technician
The local 'System' account

fix.q: How do you clear the error and start issuing IPs?
options: Right-click 'Server' in the DHCP console and select 'Authorize'
Reinstall the DHCP role
Change the server's IP address
Restart the Domain Controller

debrief.summary: Authorization prevents unauthorized people from spinning up 'Rogue' DHCP servers on a domain network.
debrief.takeaway: Authorization is an AD-level security check, not a local service status.

tickets.title: Missing Hostnames
tickets.summary: The security team says they can't track which computer is which. They see an IP in the logs, but when they check DNS, there is no name associated with it.
artifact: DHCP Server Property: 'Dynamically update DNS records' is UNCHECKED
DNS Zone: Reverse Lookup Zone (PTR) is nearly empty
Scenario: Most clients are non-Windows devices (Linux/IOT)

triage.q: Why is the DNS system failing to show names for these IPs?
options: The DNS server is offline
The DHCP server is not configured to register client names into DNS
The clients are using fake names
The network is too fast for DNS to keep up

diagnosis.q: Non-Windows devices often don't update DNS themselves. Who should do it for them in a managed network?
options: The user must type it in
The DHCP server can perform 'Proxy' updates for them
The firewall should do it
DNS updates are impossible for Linux

fix.q: Which setting will fix the lack of PTR (Reverse) records?
options: Enable 'Always dynamically update DNS records' on the DHCP server
Restart the DNS service
Delete the DHCP scope
Enable IPv6

debrief.summary: DHCP can act as a bridge, telling DNS whenever it gives an IP to a device.
debrief.takeaway: For full visibility, ensure the DHCP server is configured to update DNS records, especially for non-Windows clients.

tickets.title: The Out-of-Sync Partner
tickets.summary: You have two DHCP servers in a failover relationship. Suddenly, Server B is reporting 'Communications Interrupted' and won't issue IPs from its half of the pool.

triage.q: What stands out as a potential cause for the communication failure between the two servers?
options: One server has more RAM than the other
There is a 7-minute time difference between the two servers
Server A is newer than Server B
The failover cable is the wrong color

diagnosis.q: DHCP Failover requires tight time synchronization. What is the maximum allowed 'Time Skew' usually allowed?
options: 1 hour
60 seconds
10 minutes
24 hours

fix.q: What is the most reliable way to fix the sync issue and prevent it from recurring?
options: Manually type the correct time on both servers
Ensure both servers are syncing to the same NTP/Domain time source
Disable failover and just use one server
Reboot both servers simultaneously

debrief.summary: Failover partners use timestamps to decide who 'owns' a lease. If times are too far apart, they stop talking to avoid database corruption.
debrief.takeaway: NTP (Network Time Protocol) is the backbone of high-availability services.

tickets.title: Static IP Theft
tickets.summary: The File Server (10.10.1.10) keeps losing its network connection. When it happens, the SysAdmin notices a random iPad has joined the network and 'stolen' the IP.

triage.q: Why did the DHCP server give a client the same IP that the server is using statically?
options: The iPad is 'hacking' the network
The DHCP server has no way of knowing 10.10.1.10 is in use because it's not excluded from the pool
The file server is too old
The subnet mask is incorrect

diagnosis.q: What is the best way to define a 'No-Go Zone' for the DHCP server inside a scope?
options: An Exclusion Range
A Filter
A Policy
A Superscope

fix.q: How should the scope be adjusted to protect the servers (which use IPs .1 through .20)?
options: Add an exclusion range for 10.10.1.1 to 10.10.1.20
Reduce the scope to only 50 IPs
Give the iPad a static IP too
Turn off the DHCP server

debrief.summary: If you don't tell the DHCP server to 'stay away' from certain IPs, it will eventually hand them out.
debrief.takeaway: Exclusions are for blocks of IPs used by static devices; Reservations are for individual devices you want DHCP to manage.

tickets.title: Wrong Destination
tickets.summary: Every computer in the branch office can talk to each other, but nobody can get to the Internet. Pinging 8.8.8.8 fails with 'Destination Host Unreachable'.

triage.q: Compare the client's gateway to the actual router's IP. What is the mismatch?
options: The client is on the wrong subnet
The client is trying to send internet traffic to .254, but the router is at .1
The router is turned off
The DNS server is missing

diagnosis.q: Which DHCP Option is responsible for telling clients where the Default Gateway (Router) is?
options: Option 003 Router
Option 006 DNS
Option 015 DNS Domain Name
Option 044 WINS

fix.q: How do you restore internet access for the branch?
options: Change DHCP Option 003 to 192.168.10.1
Reboot the router
Give everyone a 10.x.x.x IP
Disable the firewall

debrief.summary: The 'Router' option (003) is the most critical setting after the IP itself. Without it, traffic never leaves the local segment.
debrief.takeaway: If internal works but external fails, check the Gateway (Option 003) first.
